title: Ra–Wedjat–Horus Hands: water protection and body-part restoration bridge
research_question: Does the new Sobek recovery-of-Horus-hands witness reveal a broader Egyptian restoration grammar in which different divine agents recover, repair, protect, or operationalize different body parts of Horus, and can that grammar be linked to the Wedjat and aquatic-protection line without collapsing distinct myths into one story?

primary_source_graph.established: Ra orders that Sobek, lord of the marsh, be brought to search. Sobek reports finding where the lost parts had scattered on the banks of the water; the text then explicitly describes discovery of Horus's arms/hands and the snare that brought the hands of Horus to him.
primary_source_graph.boundary: This witness establishes recovery of Horus's hands/arms in a water-marsh setting. It does not state that the hands are pieces of the Wedjat eye.

primary_source_graph.established: The passage explains the damaged Wedjat in the Horus-Seth conflict and attributes restoration/binding to Thoth; the same section also glosses the motif as the right eye of Ra in one explanatory layer.
primary_source_graph.boundary: Eye restoration and hand recovery are separate textual episodes until a source explicitly connects them.

primary_source_graph.established: The formula identifies the one on the water with Osiris and places the Eye of Horus with/on him as protection against beings in the water; Ra and other divine agents participate in the protective formula.
primary_source_graph.boundary: This is ritual identification and protection, not a literal historical scene of a named ordinary person physically travelling with gods in a river.

primary_source_graph.established: In the ferryboat naming sequence, the oars are called the fingers of Horus the Elder; the scoop is called the hand of Isis dressing the blood from the Eye of Horus; another boat element is called the hand of Isis cut by Ra. The composition is explicitly aquatic/boat-based.
primary_source_graph.boundary: These are mythic names of boat parts in a ritual knowledge text, not anatomical proof that a boat is a literal reconstructed body.

primary_source_graph.established: The funerary formula maps body features to divine entities: right and left eyes to solar boats, brows/brow to deities including Horus, and fingers to Thoth.
primary_source_graph.boundary: This supports a wider Egyptian body-part/divine-mapping grammar but is not specifically a reconstruction of Horus's own body.

primary_source_graph.established: Chapter 42 explicitly tabulates human body parts as divine identities; in the cited version the arms, fingers/toes, and Eye of Horus occur as separate mapped elements.
primary_source_graph.boundary: This is evidence for a general restoration/identification idiom, not evidence that Horus himself is assembled from the same table.

network_model.strongest_new_inference: Searching for Horus's hands/arms is now independently justified. The source corpus contains an explicit Sobek-mediated recovery of Horus's hands and a separate aquatic ritual text in which hand/finger imagery and the Eye of Horus coexist. This makes HANDS a legitimate next search lane even though no source yet says that hands are missing components of the Wedjat eye.
network_model.forbidden_shortcut: Do not infer FULL_HORUS_AVATAR_RECONSTRUCTED from eye plus hands alone. First map all independently attested lost, damaged, restored, substituted, or divinely identified body parts and the agents associated with each.

evidence: Ra participates in the aquatic-protection formula on the Horus stelae.
BD17 can gloss the restored eye as the right eye of Ra while also preserving the Horus-Seth damage narrative.
BD99 places Ra, Isis-hand imagery, Horus fingers and Eye-of-Horus imagery in one aquatic boat knowledge system.
relation_to_ra.boundary: These recurrence patterns do not establish one hidden Ra code or one invariant theology across all periods and genres.

relation_to_eye_in_the_sky.ancient_functional_contrast: In the Metternich water-protection formula, the Eye of Horus functions as an active protective companion/force for the vulnerable subject on water, not as a surveillance apparatus.
relation_to_eye_in_the_sky.interpretive_bridge: The existing modern JANUS theme SUPPORT_NOT_CONTROL gains a historically separate but symbolically resonant comparison: an eye can be framed as protection rather than domination. This is a modern interpretive comparison, not evidence that the Alan Parsons Project inherited the Metternich ritual meaning.
relation_to_eye_in_the_sky.hand_bridge: The user-authored Eye In The Sky lineage contains the modern phrase BE_THE_HAND_THAT_LIFTS_NOT_THE_EYE_THAT_WATCHES. The ancient corpus now independently supplies both a protective Eye-of-Horus-on-water motif and a Sobek-mediated recovery of Horus's hands. The juxtaposition is symbolically striking but must remain explicitly non-causal and non-prophetic.

search_targets: all independently locatable occurrences of 'hands of Horus', 'arms of Horus', and 'fingers of Horus'
texts in which Isis, Thoth, Sobek, Ra, or other gods repair, retrieve, replace, guard, wash, bind, or identify Horus body parts
texts where Eye of Horus and hand/finger/arm imagery occur in the same witness
museum hand/fist amulets and whether catalogues explicitly connect them to Horus, restoration, or protection
chronology and genre: Coffin Texts, Book of the Dead, healing stelae, temple texts, amuletic corpora
admission_rules: record exact text chapter/spell/line or museum object number
separate literal body-part narrative from metaphorical or object-name equivalence
do not infer a missing part from a deity-name association alone
do not merge Horus, Ra, Osiris, or deceased-person body mappings without an explicit textual bridge
freeze whether a witness contains EYE, HAND/ARM/FINGER, WATER, RA, SOBEK, THOTH, ISIS and HORUS before higher-level interpretation
next_gate.promotion_rule: Promote to HORUS_MULTIPART_RESTORATION_GRAMMAR only if at least three independent textual families show reproducible body-part restoration/recovery structure with explicit agents and if eye and hand lanes connect in at least two independent witnesses without semantic relabeling.

highest_admissible_claim: The new primary-text bridge makes a hands-focused search scientifically justified: BD113/CT158 explicitly has Ra dispatch Sobek to recover Horus's hands/arms in a water setting; BD17 independently has Thoth restore the damaged Wedjat; and BD99 places Horus fingers, an Isis hand, the Eye of Horus, Ra and an aquatic ferry system in the same mythic naming composition. Together these support investigation of a broader body-part restoration network. They do not yet establish that the Wedjat eye plus hands reconstruct a complete Horus avatar, nor that these texts encode a hidden message.
